root_cause.text: KVM/x86’s `vcpu_block()` incorrectly treated `-EBUSY` from `kvm_check_nested_events()` as a hard failure when a vCPU was in nested guest mode, so a vCPU awakened in L2 with already-injected or pending nested events could trigger an invalid userspace exit instead of continuing execution.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `vcpu_block()` from `WARN_ON_ONCE(r == -EBUSY); if (r < 0) return 0;` to `if (r < 0 && r != -EBUSY) return 0;`, and the commit message says that “Ignore -EBUSY when checking nested events after exiting a blocking state while L2 is active” because otherwise “exiting to userspace will generate a spurious userspace exit, usually with KVM_EXIT_UNKNOWN,” especially when userspace has stuffed `MP_STATE` and/or injected events into an “impossible” blocked state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop warning and prematurely returning when nested event checking reports -EBUSY, while keeping other error handling unchanged.
intent_record.what: In the nested-guest path of vcpu_block(), the code removed the unconditional WARN_ON_ONCE(r == -EBUSY) and changed the early-return condition from `if (r < 0)` to `if (r < 0 && r != -EBUSY)`, so `-EBUSY` is no longer treated as a return-triggering error there.
intent_record.how: At runtime, `kvm_check_nested_events(vcpu)` can now return `-EBUSY` without generating a warning or causing `vcpu_block()` to exit early. Other negative errors still cause the function to return 0, preserving the previous handling for genuine failures while exempting the busy case.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it stops treating -EBUSY from kvm_check_nested_events() as a fatal return path in vcpu_block(), allowing nested guests with pending/injected events to continue instead of causing an invalid userspace exit.

candidates.rationale: This line shows that -EBUSY from kvm_check_nested_events() was treated as an exceptional condition, reflecting the buggy handling of nested guest events that could lead to an invalid userspace exit.

This conditional captures the erroneous logic that any negative return from kvm_check_nested_events(), including -EBUSY in nested mode, was treated as a hard failure instead of allowing vCPU execution to continue.
This premature return is the direct consequence of misclassifying -EBUSY as fatal, causing the vCPU to exit rather than continue running with pending nested events.

This premature return was taken on -EBUSY as part of the erroneous negative-error handling, causing vCPU blocking to abort instead of continuing execution with pending nested events.
